mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC is below 0.10.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the same month indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST < previous month - 10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC falls below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% from the previous month, sustained for two consecutive months, indicates contraction in manufacturing output and suggests lower corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month - 1% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 30% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate below 1% combined with a concurrent rise in the Consumer Price Index above 4% signals a monetary policy-lag-induced inflationary environment, which erodes real corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 35% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payroll employment increase (PAYEMS) below 50,000 for three consecutive months signals persistent labor market slack, which depresses wage growth and consumer demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < previous month + 50,000 for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.15) during triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline of at least 3% in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a broad-based collapse in residential and non-residential demand, which directly reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, especially in late-cycle regimes.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < previous month - 3% AND HOUST < previous month - 3%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 25% of triggered late-cycle episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of at least 0.5% for four consecutive months, regardless of regime, signals broad-based supply chain weakness, which raises input costs and reduces output, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) in at least 70% of triggered periods.
